summary: Alberta lookout west of Sundre: a 1927 cab, a steel tower dated only to the 1960s, and a tower reserved for the observer when manned.

facts.design: Steel tower about 6 m (20 ft) high with a cupola cab, plus a three-room house for living quarters (Canada Lookouts index)

access.note: The small tower is reserved for the lookout observer when the station is manned in spring and summer. The summit is reached on foot by a logging road and a maintenance track. No source read says the public may enter the tower, and none says the site is closed.

visit.trail_note: Park near a gate at the start of an unmarked side road off the Forestry Trunk Road (940), 2.3 km east of the Red Deer Ranger station. A logging road climbs about halfway, then a narrower maintenance track leads to the top. The route guide calls the trail an old closed fire road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief gives 2003 from the Alberta lookout dataset, which was read only at metadata level. The Canada Lookouts index dates the steel tower only to the 1960s (196??), citing a 1998 guidebook. No source read gives 2003, so the story does not use it.

The brief gives 6.0 m. The index and a 2008 trip report both say 20 feet, which is 6.1 m, so 6.1 m is used. An OpenStreetMap way for the site carries a height tag of 10 on what looks like a building footprint; that is volunteer data and is not used.

notes_for_editor: The history comes mainly from one volunteer index (Canada Lookouts), which quotes a 1930 Calgary Herald item and cites a 1998 guidebook for the 1960s steel tower. The 1960 event year is a placeholder for '196??'. The brief's 2003 build date for the present structure is not in any source read and is left out; the 2008 trip report and the index both fit a tower already standing by 2008. A Facebook group post surfaced in search (snippet only, not opened) says a 1960s tower was removed at the landowner's request in 2005. That conflicts with the brief's 2003 and with a 20-foot tower photographed in 2008, so check it before publishing if the build history matters. The brief's 'closed' access is not stated by any source read; it is recorded as 'restricted' because the tower is reserved for the observer when the station is manned. A search snippet for an AllTrails listing says access should be restricted to weekends while logging is active; the page was not read, so it is not used. Agency: the brief says Alberta Wildfire, but no source read names the agency for this tower, so no agency fact is set. Six distinct pages were read, within the budget.
